answer: Sequential time tax: each epoch every earning identity must compute a verifiable delay function on that epoch's random seed, about one hour of strictly sequential squaring that extra cores cannot speed up. Any validator checks the short proof in milliseconds before the identity's answers count. One run cannot wander between identities, because each output is bound to its own key, so a hundred fakes need a hundred quartz-clocked cores busy all epoch. Limit: a rich farm can rent cores far past the horizon of a hobbyist budget, so this only prices identities and must pair with quality grading.
